column1: PREPPIEST PONY — PARTICIPANTS' FAVORITE HORSE SELECTION PROCESS
PURPOSE: Let the participants choose their favorite eligible horse while protecting the horses, the participants, and the integrity of the choice.

column3: Controlled Requirement

Identify horses participating in the applicable cycle. A horse must be medically/welfare appropriate for ordinary participant interaction. A horse on rest, treatment or showing stress may be withheld without penalty or negative designation.
column6: Participants choose the horse they personally favor from the eligible horse group.
column7: Best-looking horse; highest-value horse; fastest horse; most skilled horse; best pedigree; handler popularity contest.
column8: Preference itself is valid; no participant must justify it.

column3: Define the participant group before voting opens. Eligible participants are people who actually participated in the applicable horse/equine experience during the cycle. Staff/handlers do not receive a ballot merely because of their role unless they independently qualify as participants under the pre-set cycle rule.
column7: Eligibility limited to pony-sized animals or a conformation/grooming competition.
column8: Any eligible horse may win unless the Founder later creates a separate pony-only rule.

column3: Participants should have a reasonable ordinary opportunity to know/interact with eligible horses during the cycle. Equal forced contact or identical time is not required; horse welfare and participant choice control.
column7: The handler/trainer automatically shares or owns the award.
column8: Handlers may be credited for care separately, but participant ballots select the horse.

column3: Handlers, staff, families and supporters may not solicit votes, advertise one horse against another, repeatedly direct participants toward a horse, create special access, or use treats/rewards during the voting process to manufacture preference.
column6: Horse comfort and welfare remain a gate before and after voting.
column7: A requirement that every horse be handled equally, displayed, decorated or kept available to secure votes.
column8: A horse may rest or be removed from the ballot for welfare without stigma.

column3: Each eligible participant receives one private ballot and may select one eligible horse or abstain. No explanation, testimonial or public declaration is required.
column6: One eligible participant, one equal private ballot; abstention permitted.
column7: Social-media voting, donor voting, staff block voting, proxy voting or adult pressure on youth participants.
column8: Ballot privacy and equal voting weight are mandatory.

column3: Selection Records Steward and one independent verifier count valid ballots. Duplicate ballots, ineligible ballots and altered ballots are excluded and documented without blaming participants.
column6: Tie is resolved only by the pre-recorded neutral method.
column7: Selection Circle choosing the horse it prefers after seeing a tie.
column8: Tie procedure is recorded before ballots are opened.

column3: The eligible horse receiving the highest number of verified valid participant ballots is PREPPIEST PONY for that cycle.

If two or more eligible horses share the highest verified ballot count, use the predetermined neutral tie-break method recorded before voting; no handler, staff member or Selection Circle member may choose based on personal preference.

Before recognition, confirm the selected horse remains appropriate for participation/recognition. Recognition must not require costumes, handling, crowd exposure or presentation that compromises welfare.

Recognize the horse as the participants' favorite. Preserve aggregate ballot count, eligibility/welfare verification, tie procedure if used and process learning. Do not publish who voted for which horse.
Application

column2: Eligible participants collectively determine the favorite through ballots.
column3: Selection Circle verifies; it does not substitute its preference.
column7: No retroactive extension to favor a horse

column3: No weighted ballots based on age, role, donation, tenure, family, staff status or program performance.
column7: Record horse identifier/name only as reasonably needed

column3: Only aggregate results and necessary verification information are retained/reported.

column2: A participant may decline to vote.
column3: No one is pressured to name a favorite.

column2: Only horses eligible for responsible participant interaction enter the ballot.
column3: Removal for medical/welfare reasons is protective, not punitive.

column2: Material campaigning/manipulation triggers process review and may invalidate affected evidence/ballots.
column3: The horse itself is never penalized for a human's improper campaigning unless ballot integrity cannot be restored.
column7: Do not connect voter names to horse choice in public records

column2: Highest verified valid ballot count wins.
column3: No 80-point threshold or five-reviewer preference score applies.

column2: Predetermined neutral method resolves equal highest ballot counts.
column3: No subjective tie-breaking.
